question: Fill in the blank:As per international standards, the diameter of a table tennis ball is ____
solution:
The correct answer is __**40 millimetres**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **diameter of a table tennis ball**, as per the **International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF)**, is officially standardized at **40 millimetres**.
 
• Prior to the year **2000**, table tennis balls had a diameter of **38 millimetres**, but the size was increased to **40 millimetres** to slow down the speed of the game and make it more spectator-friendly.
 
• The material used in manufacturing table tennis balls is typically **celluloid** or similar plastic polymers to ensure uniform bounce and durability.
 
• Table tennis balls weigh approximately **2.7 grams**, and the weight and diameter are strictly regulated to maintain fairness in international competitions.
 
• The **40 millimetre ball** is designed to meet the requirements of both recreational and professional players, enhancing the overall experience of the game.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Table Tennis Evolution:**

 
 
• Table tennis originated in the late **19th century** as an indoor version of lawn tennis, and the equipment has evolved significantly since then.
 
• The **ITTF** was established in **1926** to regulate the rules, equipment, and standards of the sport.
 
• The ball size change in **2000** was a landmark decision to improve game visibility and reduce the speed of play for spectators.
 
 
 
• **ITTF Regulations:**
 
 
• The ITTF specifies that the ball must be **spherical**, with a diameter of exactly **40 millimetres**.
 
• The ball's bounce should be consistent, with a drop test from **30 cm height** resulting in a bounce of approximately **24 cm**.
 
 
 
• **Other Equipment Specifications:**
 
 
• Table tennis tables have dimensions of **2.74 metres** in length, **1.525 metres** in width, and a height of **76 centimetres**.
 
• The net height is regulated at **15.25 centimetres**.
 
 
 
• **Competitive Use:**
 
 
• The **40 millimetre ball** is mandatory for all ITTF-sanctioned tournaments, including the **Olympics**, **World Table Tennis Championships**, and other major international events.
 
• The switch to the larger ball was also aimed at promoting the sport globally by making it more accessible to beginners and amateurs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact of Ball Size Change:**

 
 
• The increase in ball diameter from **38 mm to 40 mm** slowed down the game, making it easier for spectators to follow rallies.
 
• Players had to adapt their techniques and strategies to accommodate the changes in speed and spin dynamics.
 
 
 
• **Ball Grading:**
 
 
• Table tennis balls are graded by star ratings, with **three-star balls** being the highest quality used in official competitions.
 
• Lower-grade balls are commonly used for recreational purposes due to their affordability.
 
 
 
• **Global Popularity:**
 
 
• Table tennis is one of the most popular sports globally, with over **300 million** active players.
 
• The sport is particularly prominent in countries like **China**, **Japan**, **Germany**, and **Korea**.
